event.summary: moved host probes preserve identity and final-output boundaries
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: considered whether moving lifecycle decisions from the terminal wrapper could signal a reused process, losing user-owned work, or durably classify a failed launch before its final output arrived. Original potential process-loss consequence is preserved for independent drop checking; no shipped route to such a kill was established in this move. Source checks: parent service/terminals.rs:170-239 and new hosts/terminal.rs:713-860,2554-2617 preserve the host branch. probe uses the adoption-pinned child identity; sweep_root rechecks live_root, rejects a different pid or unreadable host, and returns the existing start token rather than capturing a new identity from the probe's bare pid. Initial caller checks: Stop at service/handlers.rs:861-915 captures that tuple before durable I/O; Restart at service/core.rs:12380-12415 and tab reap at 14126-14142 use the Running-pid/sweep_root boundary. Repair-turn synthesis checked the downstream boundary: service/sweep.rs:1432-1439 passes each carried tuple to validate_root_identity; 1574-1623 compares its expected start token with the current process and rejects changed/missing identity, propagating unreadability. Delete's separate path at service/teardown.rs:320-345 uses pinned_child_root instead of this helper, and service/session_hosts.rs:510-547 pins recorded-host roots over the connection and refuses an unpinned running child. These checks bound the refutation to root construction and admission, not every signal or descendant-selection mechanism. Final-output synthesis: holds_final_state waits for processed exit evidence with the same watch/timeout loop as the old wrapper; handlers.rs:1009-1058 gates wrapper_failure_detail with final_state && dead and records a plain exit when the record has not arrived. launch_artifacts.rs:60-76 independently checks processed-exit evidence before appending screen text. Contract: SPEC_impl.md Terminal host, terminal switch points and Launch failure classification, requires pinned roots and processed exit records before terminal-based launch inference. Suggested bucket: highest if the hypothetical reused-process kill existed; other for incomplete launch-error diagnostics; no defect established. Could-be-highest: yes, unintended termination of another user-owned process was the original concern. Confidence: confirmed source-based refutation for the helper move and inspected caller/downstream boundaries; no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation, the host identity tuple survives the move and is revalidated before root admission, while final-output inference retains its processed-exit gate. possible_cover: parent reports g101/c2 independently checks preserved pinned identities; no coverage files consulted. Caveat: this is not a repository-wide proof against process loss, a proof of all lifecycle races, or validation of every later descendant signal. The original potential highest concern remains explicit for independent review.

event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: considered whether removing the orderly-stop notification strands a restart or an encoder during shutdown. Source checks: git grep over the parent found stop_began's sole waiting consumer in host_restart.rs:905-930, selecting against the tmux history-seed future; that retired branch explicitly logs reading the tmux pane's history. The new revision has no stop_began references. Host restart module docs and restart_seed at host_restart.rs:400-417 delegate encoding to the held host runtime; checkpoint_hosts_for_exit_with_slots at host_handover.rs:300-345 still sets stopping under the map lock and aborts or closes every gathered runtime. Contract: SPEC_impl.md Terminal host, Across supervisor restarts and Restarting a host agent, assigns cancellation to the host runtime. Suggested bucket: other for the suspected shutdown stall; no defect established. Could-be-highest: no established loss-of-work route in this concern. Confidence: confirmed source-based removal of an obsolete consumer; no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation, the notifier's only consumer was removed with the tmux seed path, and host cancellation is owned by its runtime. possible_cover: none. Caveat: this does not prove every shutdown timing interleaving; it rejects the missing-notification hypothesis.

event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: considered whether removing the orderly-stop notification strands a restart or its encoder during shutdown. Original suspected consequence remains a shutdown stall; no process-loss route was established for this concern. Source checks from the initial pass: the parent's sole waiting stop_began consumer was host_restart.rs:905-930, selecting against the removed tmux history-seed future. Coverage-repair synthesis followed the surviving host path into its implementation: hosts/terminal.rs:2414-2420 abort sets the runtime's shared encode-cancel flag and aborts the task; history_seed at 2443-2451 sends a Seed request and awaits its oneshot, so a dropped runtime releases the waiter. seed_now at 3733-3765 passes that same cancel flag into history_seed_until on the blocking pool, counts the encode with RunningEncode, and restores the emulator on ordinary completion. Runtime::drop at 3020-3026 sets the same cancel flag even when the task is dropped by runtime shutdown. host_restart.rs:418-478 keeps the old runtime on the session map while awaiting the seed, and a missing seed while stopping refuses the restart before generation claim; core.rs:12483-12492 requests this seed before spawning the destructive relaunch task. host_handover.rs:300-345 gathers under the session-map lock, sets stopping and aborts short-tail runtimes; its checkpoint tasks abort their runtime after the checkpoint, and close_all covers every gathered runtime. Contract: SPEC_impl.md Terminal host, Across supervisor restarts and Restarting a host agent, assigns encode cancellation to that runtime. Suggested bucket: other for the suspected stall; no defect established. Could-be-highest: no established loss-of-work route in this concern. Confidence: confirmed source-based cancellation path; no execution or timing measurement. proposed_drop: source refutation, the removed notifier served only the retired tmux seed path; the surviving host seed receives cancellation through its runtime and oneshot ownership. possible_cover: none. Caveat: bounded to notification removal and the inspected seed/abort/drop path; this is not a proof of every shutdown interleaving or a measured cancellation latency.

event.summary: marker-inheritance documentation wrongly puts tab markers on terminal hosts
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: the revised cleanup explanation tells future maintainers that terminal-host processes inherit a parent session's tab marker. They do not: the host's empty environment is the boundary that keeps Stop's marker sweep from killing the terminal process and losing its retained screen. The child receives environment entries in its launch spec instead. This is a documentation defect; no unsafe production signaling is alleged. Source: launch.rs:110-118 now says 'A supervisor running inside somebody's tab inherits that tab's FARHELM_TAB_ID, its terminal hosts inherit it, and every INNER agent it launches inherits it too' (backticks omitted here only). The parent patch explicitly replaces tmux server with terminal hosts in this sentence. hosts/spawn.rs:19-24 explains that the host's own environment is empty specifically to keep session markers and credentials off it, and the host start at :353 calls env_clear. ChildSpec.env at :117 is separately serialized at :508 onward; the child environment is not the host process environment. Correct nearby TAB_ID_ENV_VAR docs at launch.rs:85-89 expressly call it the terminal host's child environment, so they expose rather than repair the contradictory inheritance narrative. The related inline comment at launch.rs:1227-1232 uses the broader 'passes ... through its own terminal hosts' wording; fix that explanation together if needed to distinguish spec transport from process-environment inheritance. Suggested fix: describe the supervisor composing the child's environment from its own base and transporting it in the spec, while keeping the host itself marker-free; retain the actual reason the agent shim scrubs an outer tab marker. Contract: SPEC_impl.md Terminal host, Starting a host, states an empty host environment keeps session markers and credentials off the host, and the child's environment travels only in the spec. Suggested bucket: other (incorrect developer-facing ownership/cleanup explanation). Could-be-highest: no established security or user-work-loss route from this wording; host termination/lost retained output describes why the real invariant matters, not an alleged runtime defect. Confidence: confirmed by pinned comment and source, no execution. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none in supplied neighboring findings. Caveats: marker scrubbing and positive agent selection may be correct production behavior; that does not refute the false host-inheritance statement. Whole-range/later-edit status is being checked next; this charter includes the recorded intermediate commit.
